summary: IgnisZero v3.0 is an interactive System Identification (SI) digital twin and autonomous fire-safety command center engineered to protect spacecraft crews from microgravity combustion hazards. Calibrated across 500 flight and parabolic-flight regimes from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database—spanning Solid (BASS), Liquid droplet (FLEX cool flames), and Gaseous jet (SPICE) combustion—IgnisZero predicts spherical flame spread velocity, runs 1,000-trial Monte Carlo uncertainty envelopes, detects ultrafine 45 nm smoke aerosols 66 seconds faster than ceiling thermistors (SAME-R telemetry), and simulates automated ECLSS fan isolation and CO2 quenching inside a 3D spacecraft habitat—especially under high-risk 34% O2 Artemis Lunar Gateway atmospheres.
details: ### The Microgravity Fire Hazard In 0g spaceflight environments, the absence of natural buoyancy fundamentally alters fire physics. Flames expand outward as near-spherical diffusion zones rather than rising plumes, hot combustion gases stagnate instead of rising to ceiling smoke detectors, and NASA’s upcoming Artemis Lunar Gateway exploration atmosphere (34% O2, 56.5 kPa) accelerates solid flame spread velocity more than fivefold compared to the ISS (21% O2, 101.3 kPa). ### What IgnisZero v3.0 Does IgnisZero v3.0 transforms NASA empirical microgravity combustion research into a real-time mission-planning and flight-operations digital twin for Team TetraHack: 1. **Multi-Phase System Identification Engine (Solid / Liquid / Gas):** Predicts flame spread velocity (mm/s), Flammability Risk Index (LOW / ELEVATED / CRITICAL), and time-to-quench across Solid polymers (BASS), Liquid fuel droplets and cool-flame regimes (FLEX), and Gaseous jet flames (SPICE), calibrated across 500 NASA PSI test runs. 2. **Interactive 3D Spacecraft Habitat & Autonomous Suppression Twin:** Visualizes 3D flame geometry, cabin ventilation distortion, and automated ECLSS mitigation—isolating cabin circulation fans at T+25s and injecting a CO2 dilution wave to drive local oxygen below the material Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI). 3. **1,000-Run Monte Carlo Uncertainty & 2D Phase-Space Heatmap:** Propagates real-time sensor telemetry noise through 1,000 stochastic simulations to compute 95% confidence intervals alongside an O2-by-Airflow phase-space map separating safe quench zones from runaway combustion. 4. **SAME-R Multi-Sensor Early Aerosol Telemetry:** Simulates avionics PTFE wire short-circuits releasing ultrafine 45 nm smoke aerosols, proving that duct optical aerosol and CO/HCN gas sensors trigger 66 seconds earlier than legacy ceiling thermistors in 0g. 5. **Aerospace Material Qualification & Flight-Ops Certification Export:** Benchmarks Nomex, Ultem, Kevlar, Kapton, and SIBAL under 34% O2 Artemis atmospheres, exposes all 500 calibrated NASA PSI regimes, includes an AI Research Copilot grounded in FLEX/BASS/SAME-R literature, and exports a downloadable NASA Flight-Ops Fire Safety Certification brief in one click. ### How It Was Built Built in Python using Streamlit, NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, and Plotly 3D WebGL rendering, deployed continuously on Streamlit Community Cloud with full open-source code hosted on GitHub.
